summary: Dropbox provides a robust OAuth 2.0 implementation supporting PKCE and multiple grant types. Developers must register apps in the App Console, configure redirect URIs, and follow specific security guidelines regarding web-views and scope selection to ensure a smooth integration process.

access_ladder.name: Development
access_ladder.allows: The developer can configure the app to access only its own folder or the entire Dropbox account.

claims.text: Apps can be configured to access only their own folder or the entire Dropbox account.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable for apps that export content or manage only their content. Full Dropbox: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on all data within the user’s Dropbox account.

access_ladder.name: Review
access_ladder.allows: The developer must ensure requested scopes and content access are minimal to avoid user rejection and pass the app review process.

claims.text: Requesting more scope and content access than required may result in end users not accepting your OAuth request and could impact your app review process.

claim.text: Uncheck the Only me box in the Visibility section to enable the Extension for other users.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Once you have configured the Extension settings and have carried out tests to ensure that the Extension works as you intended, you can return to this field and uncheck the Only me box to enable the Extension for other users.

claim.text: Users must authorize the app via OAuth before the extension shows in their menu.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Extensions will not show in “Open” or “Share” menu of the end user until a) you have unchecked the “Only me” box under “Visibility” section of the app and b) the user authorizes the app via OAuth*.

extras.title: Choices to make before you start (token / app / registration types)
extras.why_it_matters: The provider offers more than one way to set up. Compare before you choose.

claims.text: User Authentication uses an access token for a specific user and app pair.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: This type uses an access token for a specific user and app pair, in order to operate on that user’s account, to the extent allowed by that app’s permission.

claims.text: Team Authentication uses an access token for a specific team and app pair.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: This type uses an access token for a specific team and app pair, in order to operate on that team, to the extent allowed by that app’s permissions.

claims.text: App Authentication uses the app's own key and secret or an app auth token without identifying a specific user or team.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: This type can either use the app’s own app key and secret, or an app auth token. This type of authentication doesn’t identify a specific user or team.

claims.text: Dropbox offers two content access types: App Folder and Full Dropbox.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable for apps that export content or manage only their content. Full Dropbox: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on all data within the user’s Dropbox account.

claims.text: PKCE is an extension to OAuth 2.0 that uses dynamic codes instead of a static client_secret.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: PKCE is an open extension to OAuth 2.0, and solves this problem using dynamic codes instead of the static client_secret.

claims.text: The DBX Platform provides APIs for building custom solutions.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: DBX Platform enables you to leverage our robust set of APIs to build custom solutions that improve collaboration, streamline workflows, and secure content.

claims.text: Dropbox recommends using one of the Dropbox SDKs when possible.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Using one of these SDKs is recommended when possible.
